flat.name: Arizona
flat.note: 2.5% after the standard deduction published for 2025. $100 credit per dependent.

flat.name: Colorado
flat.note: 4.4% after the 2025 standard deduction in the Tax Foundation table.

flat.name: Georgia
flat.note: 5.19% after H.B. 111, which lowered the 2025 rate retroactively. $4,000 exemption per dependent.

flat.name: Idaho
flat.note: 5.3% after H.B. 40, retroactive to January 1, 2025. Rate applies above the zero-rate band.

flat.name: Illinois
flat.note: 4.95% after the personal exemption. No standard deduction.

flat.name: Indiana
flat.note: 3% after the personal exemption. County tax is not included; enter it as a local rate if you want it in the estimate.

flat.name: Iowa
flat.note: 3.8% of AGI, minus the small personal exemption credit. The 2025 compiled table does not list a standard deduction.

flat.name: Michigan
flat.note: 4.25% after the personal exemption. City income tax is not included.

flat.name: Mississippi
flat.note: 4.4% above $10,000 after the standard deduction and personal exemption.

flat.name: Pennsylvania
flat.note: 3.07% of AGI. Pennsylvania does not allow a standard deduction or personal exemption. Local earned-income tax is not included.

flat.name: Utah
flat.note: 4.5% after H.B. 106, retroactive to January 1, 2025. The taxpayer credit is a flat published amount and does not phase out in this estimate.

ohio.name: Ohio
ohio.note: 2025 IT 1040 brackets and the booklet's inflation-adjusted exemptions. Joint filing credit assumes each spouse has at least $500 of qualifying income.
